'''Metiria Leanne Agnes Stanton Turei''' (born 1970) is a New Zealand academic and former politician. She was a Member of [[New Zealand House of Representatives|Parliament]] from 2002 to 2017, and the female [[Co-leaders of the Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand|co-leader]] of the [[Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand]] from 2009 to 2017. Turei resigned from the co-leader position on 9 August 2017 amid a political controversy arising from her admission to lying to the [[Ministry of Social Development (New Zealand)|Ministry of Social Development]] to receive higher payments when she was on the [[Domestic Purposes Benefit]], and later, to being enrolled to vote in an electorate where she was not eligible when she was 23.<ref name="rnz-turei-resigns" /> <!--the details of the fraud-related controversy are further down in the article.-->

She was the Green Party spokesperson on Inequality, Justice, and Building and Housing.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.greens.org.nz/ourpeople/metiria-turei-mp|title=Metiria Turei MP|website=Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand|language=en|access-date=1 April 2017|archive-date=6 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170406131419/https://www.greens.org.nz/ourpeople/metiria-turei-mp|url-status=live}}</ref> She resigned as co-leader of the Green Party and a list candidate immediately prior to the 2017 general election, and retired from politics.<ref name="auto">{{cite web|url=http://www.radionz.co.nz/news/political/340115/metiria-turei-bows-out|title=Metiria Turei bows out|date=24 September 2017|website=Radionz.co.nz|access-date=14 November 2017|archive-date=20 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171120081403/http://www.radionz.co.nz/news/political/340115/metiria-turei-bows-out|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Early years==
Metiria Turei grew up in a working-class [[Māori people|Māori]] family in [[Palmerston North]] in the [[North Island]].{{Sfn|Turei|2017|pp=178–179}} She is of [[Ngāti Kahungunu]] and Āti Hau nui a Pāpārangi descent.<ref name=WAC1/> She failed her high school examinations and in 1987 she worked her first job as a kitchen-hand at the [[Hard Rock Café]] in Palmerston North working the late shift.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/politics/news/article.cfm?c_id=280&objectid=11766244 |title=My Summer Job: Green Party co-leader Metiria Turei |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=28 December 2016 |access-date=28 December 2016 |archive-date=28 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161228112309/http://www.nzherald.co.nz/politics/news/article.cfm?c_id=280&objectid=11766244 |url-status=live }}</ref> Between 1989 and 1991, Turei was the ''Tumuaki'' ("Head") of Te Iwi Maori Rawakore o Aotearoa{{efn|Te Iwi Maori Rawakore o Aotearoa is a group whose name translates approximately as "The Impoverished Māori of New Zealand"}} and involved with Te Roopu Rawakore o Aotearoa. Turei was a founding member of the [[Random Trollops]] performance art troupe.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA0307/S00272/a-random-trollop-to-rock-the-house.htm|title=A Random Trollop to rock the House {{!}} Scoop News|website=Scoop.co.nz|access-date=1 April 2017|archive-date=1 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170401145211/http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA0307/S00272/a-random-trollop-to-rock-the-house.htm|url-status=live}}</ref> She studied law at the [[University of Auckland]] and later worked as a commercial lawyer at [[Simpson Grierson]].{{Sfn|Turei|2017|pp=184–193}}

==Political career==
She was a candidate for the [[McGillicuddy Serious Party]] in the [[1993 New Zealand general election|1993 election]], for the [[Aotearoa Legalise Cannabis Party]] in the [[1996 New Zealand general election|1996 election]] and for McGillicuddy Serious again in the [[1999 New Zealand general election|1999 election]]. In [[2001 Auckland City mayoral election|2001]] she stood as the Green Party candidate for [[Mayor of Auckland City|Mayor of Auckland]], finishing a distant fifth with 2.05% of the vote.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aucklandcity.govt.nz/council/governing_your_city/election_2001/results.asp |title=Final Official Election Results |access-date=11 July 2017 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020627043145/http://www.aucklandcity.govt.nz/council/governing_your_city/election_2001/results.asp |archive-date=27 June 2002 }}</ref>

In the [[2002 New Zealand general election|2002 general election]], the [[Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand|Green Party]] received 7.00% of the vote, which allowed them 9 seats in [[New Zealand Parliament|Parliament]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2002/|title=2002 GENERAL ELECTION – OFFICIAL RESULT|website=archive.electionresults.govt.nz|access-date=1 April 2017|archive-date=7 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170407083115/http://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2002/|url-status=live}}</ref> Turei, standing in {{NZ electorate link|Tāmaki Makaurau}}, was ranked 8th on the Green Party's [[Party-list proportional representation|party list]], and so entered Parliament as a [[list MP]]. When she was elected, Turei left her job as a corporate lawyer for [[Simpson Grierson]] to become a Member of Parliament.

She retained her place in Parliament ranked 6th on the Greens' list in the [[2005 New Zealand general election|2005 election]] when she stood in {{NZ electorate link|Te Tai Tonga}}.

====2005–2008====
In 2009, Turei's [https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/bills-and-laws/bills-proposed-laws/document/00DBHOH_BILL7386_1/misuse-of-drugs-medicinal-cannabis-amendment-bill Misuse of Drugs (Medicinal Cannabis) Amendment Bill] was drawn from the member's ballot.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.parliament.nz/en-NZ/PB/Legislation/Bills/5/7/2/00DBHOH_BILL7386_1-Misuse-of-Drugs-Medicinal-Cannabis-Amendment-Bill.htm |title=Misuse of Drugs (Medicinal Cannabis) Amendment Bill |publisher=New Zealand Parliament |access-date=8 December 2009 |archive-date=18 October 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081018071545/http://www.parliament.nz/en-NZ/PB/Legislation/Bills/5/7/2/00DBHOH_BILL7386_1-Misuse-of-Drugs-Medicinal-Cannabis-Amendment-Bill.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>  The bill received a conscience vote at its first reading, but was defeated 84–34.<ref>''New Zealand Parliamentary Debates'' '''655''' 4850.</ref>  Later that year, her Liquor Advertising (Television and Radio) Bill was also drawn, but it too was defeated.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.parliament.nz/en-NZ/PB/Legislation/Bills/d/f/7/00DBHOH_BILL7629_1-Liquor-Advertising-Television-and-Radio-Bill.htm |title=Liquor Advertising (Television and Radio) Bill |publisher=New Zealand Parliament |access-date=10 December 2009 |archive-date=18 October 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081018170334/http://www.parliament.nz/en-NZ/PB/Legislation/Bills/d/f/7/00DBHOH_BILL7629_1-Liquor-Advertising-Television-and-Radio-Bill.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[File:Metiria Turei.jpg|thumb|left|Turei in 2008]]
In [[2008 New Zealand general election|2008]] she was ranked 4th on the Green Party's list and stood in the [[Dunedin North (New Zealand electorate)|Dunedin North]] electorate. She lost the election in [[Dunedin North (New Zealand electorate)|Dunedin North]] to [[Labour Party (New Zealand)|Labour]]'s [[Pete Hodgson]], finishing third with 11.09%<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2008/electorate-8.html|title=Official Count Results – Dunedin North|website=archive.electionresults.govt.nz|access-date=1 April 2017|archive-date=9 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170409231515/http://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2008/electorate-8.html|url-status=live}}</ref> of the vote. However she was returned to parliament due to her high ranking on the Green Party list.

====2008–2011====
On 30 May 2009 Turei was elected as the fourth co-leader (and second female co-leader) of the Green Party. [[green politics|Green Party policy]] at the time required that there be both a male and a female co-leader. She was elected ahead of veteran MP [[Sue Bradford]].

In July 2009 Turei's [https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/bills-and-laws/bills-proposed-laws/document/00DBHOH_BILL9283_1/marine-animals-protection-law-reform-bill Marine Animals Protection Law Reform Bill], intended to strengthen protection for dolphins and other marine mammals, was drawn from the member's ballot.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.parliament.nz/en-NZ/PB/Legislation/Bills/1/8/6/00DBHOH_BILL9283_1-Marine-Animals-Protection-Law-Reform-Bill.htm |title=Marine Animals Protection Law Reform Bill |publisher=New Zealand Parliament |access-date=8 December 2009 |archive-date=31 July 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090731235945/http://www.parliament.nz/en-NZ/PB/Legislation/Bills/1/8/6/00DBHOH_BILL9283_1-Marine-Animals-Protection-Law-Reform-Bill.htm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.greens.org.nz/press-releases/new-bill-good-news-dolphins-and-fishing-industry |title=New Bill good news for dolphins and fishing industry |publisher=Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand |date=2 July 2009 |access-date=8 December 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100522043040/http://www.greens.org.nz/press-releases/new-bill-good-news-dolphins-and-fishing-industry |archive-date=22 May 2010  }}</ref> The bill was defeated at its first reading later that month.<ref>''New Zealand Parliamentary Debates'' '''656''' 5273.</ref>

In September 2009 Turei led the Green campaign opposing the government's plans to allow mining in New Zealand's [[National parks of New Zealand|national parks]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.greens.org.nz/press-releases/kiwis-can-speak-out-mining |title=Kiwis can speak out on mining |publisher=Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand |date=2 September 2009 |access-date=8 December 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091223041806/http://www.greens.org.nz/press-releases/kiwis-can-speak-out-mining |archive-date=23 December 2009  }}</ref> Her [https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/bills-and-laws/bills-proposed-laws/document/00DBHOH_BILL9854_1/crown-minerals-protection-of-public-conservation-land Crown Minerals (Protection of Public Conservation Land Listed in the Fourth Schedule) Amendment Bill], which aimed to strengthen the protection for national parks, was drawn from the member's ballot in April 2010.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.parliament.nz/en-NZ/PB/Legislation/Bills/e/6/4/00DBHOH_BILL9854_1-Crown-Minerals-Protection-of-Public-Conservation.htm |title=Crown Minerals (Protection of Public Conservation Land Listed in the Fourth Schedule) Amendment Bill |publisher=New Zealand Parliament |access-date=22 April 2010 |archive-date=22 May 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100522085800/http://www.parliament.nz/en-NZ/PB/Legislation/Bills/e/6/4/00DBHOH_BILL9854_1-Crown-Minerals-Protection-of-Public-Conservation.htm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/politics/news/article.cfm?c_id=280&objectid=10640108 |title=Greens' bill protecting conservation land drawn from ballot |work=The New Zealand Herald |date=22 April 2010 |access-date=22 April 2010 |archive-date=22 October 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121022234837/http://www.nzherald.co.nz/politics/news/article.cfm?c_id=280&objectid=10640108 |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2011–2014====
In October 2012 her [https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/bills-and-laws/bills-proposed-laws/document/00DBHOH_BILL11854_1/criminal-proceeds-recovery-act-2009-application-to-casinos Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009 (Application to Casinos) Amendment bill] was drawn from the ballot. Before its first reading however, National, ACT and United Future said they would not be voting for it.<ref>{{cite news| url= http://www.3news.co.nz/Casino-crime-bill-doomed-to-fail/tabid/1607/articleID/276742/Default.aspx| work= 3 News NZ| title= Casino crime bill doomed to fail| date= 15 November 2012}}{{Dead link|date=December 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Turei, along with the rest of the Green Party, voted in support of [[Marriage (Definition of Marriage) Amendment Act 2013]], allowing same-sex couples to legally marry in New Zealand.<ref>{{cite news|title=Marriage equality bill – How MPs voted|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/data/8564068/Marriage-equality-bill-How-MPs-voted|access-date=3 December 2016|work=[[Stuff.co.nz]]|date=17 April 2013|author=Harkanwal Singh|author2=Andy Ball|archive-date=24 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924134543/http://www.stuff.co.nz/data/8564068/Marriage-equality-bill-How-MPs-voted|url-status=live}}</ref>

====2017 general election====
[[File:I stand with Metiria activists.jpg|200px|thumb|Political activists with banners saying "I stand with Metiria"]]
During the [[2017 New Zealand general election|2017 election]] campaign, Turei publicly stated during an interview on [[Television New Zealand|TVNZ]]'s Q+A Show that the [[New Zealand First]] leader [[Winston Peters]] "was on a roll partly because of a very racist approach to immigration." Her comments triggered fierce criticism from Peters and NZ First Deputy Leader [[Tracey Martin]], who rejected Turei's claims and warned that there would be consequences for the Greens in any post-election talks with NZ First. Turei refused to apologise and reiterated that the Greens were still committed to negotiating a coalition deal with NZ First following the election.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Trevett|first1=Claire|title=Green Party's Metiria Turei 'racist' call riles NZ First's Winston Peters|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11888053|access-date=11 October 2017|newspaper=New Zealand Herald|date=9 July 2017|archive-date=11 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171011182436/http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11888053|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 16 July 2017, during the launch of the Green Party's 2017 election campaign, Turei admitted to benefit fraud over a period of three years in the early 1990s, stating that she had not disclosed to [[Ministry of Social Development (New Zealand)|Work and Income New Zealand]] that she was accepting rent from flatmates. Turei justified her action on the grounds that she and her young daughter depended on the [[Domestic Purposes Benefit]] to survive. During the campaign, Turei advocated raising the domestic purposes benefit for solo parents and low-income families.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kirk |first1=Stacey |title=Benefit raise, tax cuts for poorest and hikes for wealthy in new Greens policy |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/94777073/benefit-raise-tax-cuts-for-poorest-and-hikes-for-wealthy-in-news-greens-policy |access-date=26 July 2017 |work=[[Stuff.co.nz]] |date=16 July 2017 |archive-date=30 July 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170730122712/https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/94777073/benefit-raise-tax-cuts-for-poorest-and-hikes-for-wealthy-in-news-greens-policy |url-status=live }}</ref> Turei's disclosure attracted polarising responses from other politicians, the New Zealand media, and blogosphere, and criticism from Social Development Minister [[Anne Tolley]], [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour Party]] leader [[Andrew Little (New Zealand politician)|Andrew Little]], and media commentators [[Barry Soper]] and [[Patrick Gower]].<ref name="Stuff 26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170729173611/http://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2017/07/i-am-metiria-beneficiaries-share-struggles-with-winz.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> and she said she had spoken with other beneficiaries who had been withholding information about their benefit status from Work and Income.<ref name="Stuff 26 July 2017" /> Turei also advocated an amnesty on beneficiaries, while acknowledging that she had not been aware of an amnesty instituted during the 1990s.<ref>{{cite news |title=Greens' Turei calls for amnesty for beneficiaries who break law |url=http://www.radionz.co.nz/news/political/335828/greens-turei-calls-for-amnesty-for-beneficiaries-who-break-law |access-date=26 July 2017 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=26 July 2017 |archive-date=26 July 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170726025702/http://www.radionz.co.nz/news/political/335828/greens-turei-calls-for-amnesty-for-beneficiaries-who-break-law |url-status=live }}</ref> On 26 July 2017, Turei announced that she would be meeting with the Ministry of Social Development's investigative unit to calculate how much she would pay back in compensation.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Jones |first1=Nicholas |title=Metiria Turei to pay back what she owes |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11895318 |access-date=26 July 2017 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=26 July 2017 |archive-date=26 July 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170726120959/http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11895318 |url-status=live }}</ref> It was then revealed that in 1993 Turei had been enrolled to vote at the same address as her child's father. Turei denied living with the father, which would have disqualified her eligibility for the domestic purposes benefit. She stated that she had enrolled at that address in order to vote for a friend; such conduct constitutes an offence under the Electoral Act.<ref>{{cite news |title=Labour to assess whether Metiria Turei's electoral revelations could damage party |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11898744 |access-date=12 August 2017 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=4 August 2017 |archive-date=8 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808034920/http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11898744 |url-status=live }}</ref>{{request quotation|date=August 2017}}

On 7 August 2017,<ref>{{cite press release |url= https://m.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA1708/S00139/james-shaw-on-kennedy-graham-and-david-clendon.htm |title= Statement from James Shaw on Kennedy Graham and David Clendon |date= 7 August 2017 |access-date= 8 August 2017 |publisher= [[Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand]] |agency= [[Scoop (website)|Scoop]] |archive-date= 8 August 2017 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170808114826/https://m.scoop.co.nz/stories/PA1708/S00139/james-shaw-on-kennedy-graham-and-david-clendon.htm |url-status= live }}</ref> Green Party MPs [[David Clendon]] and [[Kennedy Graham]] announced that they were planning to resign as Green Party candidates for the 2017 election, due to the fraud revelations and Turei's handling of the resulting situation.<ref name="graham-clendon-rnz-1" /> Both Clendon and Graham resigned from the party caucus the following day,<ref>{{cite news |url= https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/95549623/greens-in-crisis-metiria-turei-stays-on-despite-mps-quitting |title= Rogue Green MPs withdraw from caucus – party 'united' behind co-leader Metiria Turei |access-date= 8 August 2017 |date= 8 August 2017 |work= [[Stuff.co.nz]] |archive-date= 8 August 2017 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170808074702/https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/95549623/greens-in-crisis-metiria-turei-stays-on-despite-mps-quitting |url-status= live }}</ref> after the party made moves to remove them.<ref name="graham-clendon-rnz-1">{{cite news |url= http://www.radionz.co.nz/news/top/336665/video-green-party-in-chaos-after-two-mps-rebel |title= Green Party in chaos after two MPs rebel |access-date= 8 August 2017 |date= 8 August 2017 |work= [[Radio New Zealand]] |first1= Jane |last1= Patterson |first2= Craig |last2= McCulloch |archive-date= 7 August 2017 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170807234939/http://www.radionz.co.nz/news/top/336665/video-green-party-in-chaos-after-two-mps-rebel |url-status= live }}</ref>

Turei resigned as co-leader of the Green Party and as a [[Party lists in the 2017 New Zealand general election#Greens|list candidate]] for the 2017 election on 9 August 2017, saying that the "scrutiny on [her] family has become unbearable."<ref name="rnz-turei-resigns">{{Cite news|url=http://www.radionz.co.nz/news/political/336828/live-metiria-turei-resigns-as-green-party-co-leader|title=Metiria Turei resigns as Green Party co-leader|date=9 August 2017|publisher=[[Radio New Zealand]]|access-date=9 August 2017|language=en-nz|archive-date=9 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170809051852/http://www.radionz.co.nz/news/political/336828/live-metiria-turei-resigns-as-green-party-co-leader|url-status=live}}</ref> She stated that her intention was to not return to Parliament after the election.<ref name="rnz-turei-resigns" /> Not being on the list meant that, if she failed to win the electorate of [[Te Tai Tonga]] where she was standing, she would not return to Parliament after the election. During August, the Green party fell in opinion polls to around the 5% threshold, below which there wouldn't be representation in Parliament, and Labour's new leader, [[Jacinda Ardern]], generated such a turnaround that by the end of the month, Labour overtook National in the ratings.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Young |first1=Audrey |title=English in fine fettle despite prospect of second historic loss |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/politics/news/article.cfm?c_id=280&objectid=11915748 |access-date=2 September 2017 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=2 September 2017 |archive-date=2 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170902051712/http://www.nzherald.co.nz/politics/news/article.cfm?c_id=280&objectid=11915748 |url-status=live }}</ref> In its 26 August edition, the ''[[New Zealand Listener]]'' summarised the situation as follows:<ref>{{cite news|last1=de Lore|first1=Clare|title=The Greens' James Shaw on Metiria, the election and meeting his dad a third time|url=http://www.noted.co.nz/currently/profiles/the-greens-james-shaw-on-metiria-the-election-and-meeting-his-dad-a-third-time/|access-date=2 September 2017|work=Noted.co.nz|date=19 August 2017|archive-date=2 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170902050358/http://www.noted.co.nz/currently/profiles/the-greens-james-shaw-on-metiria-the-election-and-meeting-his-dad-a-third-time/|url-status=live}}</ref>

{{Cquote|text=Metiria Turei's spectacular own goal in admitting to benefit and electoral fraud not only effectively ended her career but also took down two of her colleagues, savaged a healthy poll rating and led to Labour's changing of the guard and reversal of fortunes.|author=Clare de Lore |source=''[[New Zealand Listener]]''}}

The media outcry over the case and extensive coverage given to the benefit fraud by the mainstream media in New Zealand has led to claims of political agendas being promoted by the media. Specifically the case has been contrasted with that of [[Bill English]] (and the relative lack of media and public "outrage"), and to a lesser extent, that of [[John Key]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thespinoff.co.nz/politics/09-08-2017/the-sins-of-metiria-bill-and-john-sense-checking-the-fact-checkers/|title=The sins of Metiria, Bill and John: sense-checking the fact checkers|date=9 August 2017|website=Thespinoff.co.nz|access-date=14 November 2017|archive-date=13 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171113084946/https://thespinoff.co.nz/politics/09-08-2017/the-sins-of-metiria-bill-and-john-sense-checking-the-fact-checkers/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newsroom.co.nz/@future-learning/2017/08/15/42725/nzs-hypocrisy-on-benefit-fraud-vs-tax-evasion|title=Benefit fraud vs tax evasion: NZ's hypocrisy|date=16 August 2017|website=Newsroom.co.nz|access-date=14 November 2017|archive-date=9 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170909053513/https://www.newsroom.co.nz/@future-learning/2017/08/15/42725/nzs-hypocrisy-on-benefit-fraud-vs-tax-evasion|url-status=live}}</ref>

According to ''[[The Spinoff]]'' journalist [[Madeleine Chapman]], Turei's resignation had come as a result of Ardern sending two members of her team, rumoured to be [[Grant Robertson]] and her chief of staff Neale Jones, to inform Greens co-leader Shaw and his team that Ardern would not be giving Turei a cabinet or ministerial position within a potential Labour government. As a face&ndash;saving measure, Turei had organised her own press conference where she announced that she would not ask for a ministerial position in a Labour&ndash;led government but would remain co-leader of the Greens until the 2017 election.{{sfn|Chapman|2020|pp=93–94}}

During the 2017 election, Turei contested the [[Te Tai Tonga]] [[Māori electorates|Māori electorate]] (which covers Wellington and the entire South Island). She was defeated by Labour's candidate [[Rino Tirikatene]]<ref>{{cite news|title=Turei tells supporters she has no regrets|url=https://www.odt.co.nz/news/election-2017/turei-tells-supporters-she-has-no-regrets|newspaper=[[Otago Daily Times]]|date=23 September 2017|access-date=14 November 2017|archive-date=9 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171009143642/https://www.odt.co.nz/news/election-2017/turei-tells-supporters-she-has-no-regrets|url-status=live}}</ref> and retired from politics.<ref name="auto"/>

== Life after politics ==
In October 2018, Metiria Turei gave her first interview since leaving politics. During the interview, she revealed that she is studying art at the [[Otago Polytechnic|Dunedin School of Art]], and has work entered in a group show "wā o mua" at the [[The Blue Oyster Art Project Space|Blue Oyster Art Project Space]] in Dunedin.<ref>{{Cite news |first=Waveney |last=Russ |url=https://thespinoff.co.nz/atea/03-10-2018/metiria-turei-beyond-politics/ |title=Metiria Turei: Beyond politics |date=3 October 2018 |work=The Spinoff |access-date=3 October 2018 |archive-date=3 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181003101525/https://thespinoff.co.nz/atea/03-10-2018/metiria-turei-beyond-politics/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Her futurist art collection ''tūruapō'' was exhibited at The Wallace Arts Centre in Auckland in 2021.<ref name=WAC1>{{cite web |url=https://www.wallaceartstrust.org.nz/exhibitions/metiria-stanton-turei |title=Metiria Stanton Turei: Tūruapō |publisher=The Wallace Arts Trust |access-date=2 February 2022}}</ref>

As of 2025, Turei lectures in law at the University of Otago.<ref name="staffpage">[https://www.otago.ac.nz/law/staff/metiria-stanton-turei Metria Stanton Turei] staff page on University of Otago website, viewed 29 May 2025</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Husband |first=Dale |date=26 February 2022 |title=Metiria Turei and her new world |url=https://e-tangata.co.nz/korero/metiria-turei-and-her-new-world/ |access-date=4 March 2022 |website=E-Tangata |language=en-NZ}}</ref> In 2026 she was promoted to associate professor.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Carolino |first=Bernise |date=15 December 2025 |title=University of Otago law professor promotions: Anna High, Jeanne Snelling, Metiria Stanton Turei |url=https://www.thelawyermag.com/nz/news/general/university-of-otago-law-professor-promotions-anna-high-jeanne-snelling-metiria-stanton-turei/559880 |publisher=NZ Lawyer}}</ref> She writes a regular political column in the ''[[Otago Daily Times]]''.<ref name="staffpage"/>

==Personal life==
Metiria Turei has a daughter, Piupiu Turei, and is married to Warwick Stanton.<ref name="Newshub 23/07/17" /><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.womensweekly.co.nz/latest/real-life/metiria-turei-my-daughter-saved-me-12878 |title=Metiria Turei: My daughter saved me |work=New Zealand Woman's Weekly |access-date=2 November 2011 |archive-date=27 September 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160927131015/http://www.womensweekly.co.nz/latest/real-life/metiria-turei-my-daughter-saved-me-12878 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/5889368/Hanging-out-with-the-political-Wags|title=Hanging out with the political Wags|website=Stuff|date=2 November 2011|language=en|access-date=13 October 2018|archive-date=21 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181021164030/http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/5889368/Hanging-out-with-the-political-Wags|url-status=live}}</ref> In February 2014, Turei and her husband were living in [[Waitati]], close to the shore of [[Blueskin Bay]], a coastal estuary to the north of [[Dunedin]]. She is also a performing arts enthusiast and participated in a performing group called Random Trollops and medieval reenactments at her Blueskin Bay home.<ref>{{cite news|last1=McAvinue|first1=Shawn|title=Metiria opens 'castle' doors|url=https://www.odt.co.nz/news/dunedin/metiria-opens-castle-doors|newspaper=[[Otago Daily Times]]|date=3 February 2014|access-date=14 November 2017|archive-date=12 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170912055834/https://www.odt.co.nz/news/dunedin/metiria-opens-castle-doors|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Metiria Turei's road to Parliament came on back of colourful and often hard early life|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11901155|newspaper=New Zealand Herald|date=9 August 2017|access-date=14 November 2017|archive-date=19 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170919034212/http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11901155|url-status=live}}</ref>
